customize.desc: The Eleventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Childe. His real name is Ajax.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd780>About The Rooster</color>
I don't know what his motivations could be, but he seems genuine about wanting to help me. He treats me just like family. Oh, and speaking of family - Tonia and Teucer are always telling me about the pastries and other gifts he brings them when they write. So while I've been away form Snezhnaya, he's kept his promise to take care of my family.

<color=#ffd780>Character Story 5</color>
By the time he returned home, the young man was no longer the same.
He was no longer frightened and hesitant but had become frivolous and confident. He acted as if this world revolved around him, and as if battle existed for his sake.
Conflict often brings about change, and this capricious, incalculable change attracted Ajax like a revolving kaleidoscope.
In the eyes of his father, that third son that he had so worried about had changed for the worse, bringing much uncalled-for havoc to the seaside village of Morepesok.
Or perhaps it would be more accurate to say that Ajax had become a nexus of strife, for no matter where he went, fights and squabbles would follow — and he reveled in it.
Ultimately, after a huge brawl was pacified with some difficulty and with some near-fatal misses, his father had no choice but to hand his beloved son over for conscription into the Fatui.
He hoped that the strict military training of the Fatui could hone his son's temper, but wound up watching fully-armed troops getting the stuffing beaten out of them by a mere child.
This was a great disappointment to his father, but it also caught the attention of Pulcinella, the 5th Harbinger.
Shocked by Ajax's great strength and curious about how he invariably became the eye of a vortex of discord, Pulcinella inducted Ajax into the Fatui under the pretext of meting out punishment, ordering him to start from the bottom and take up the duty of serving the Tsaritsa.
His insatiable desire for conquest would thus be constantly satiated in fighting for the Fatui, and his ever-burgeoning ego would gorge upon the elation of vanquishing mighty foes...
Until at last, Ajax was chosen to be one of the Fatui Harbingers, donning the mantle of "Childe" Tartaglia and becoming one of the most powerful people in Snezhnaya.
But becoming Tartaglia was far from his end goal. To someone who sought to conquer the world, this was but a tiny step in his journey.

customize.name: Tartaglia
customize.desc: The Eleventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Childe. His real name is Ajax.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd780>About Arlecchino</color>
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : I've met some of the members of your organization, and they all seemed like really good kids. They actually reminded me of Tonia and Teucer.
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : Which, by the way, if you ever betray them, I'm just letting you know — I won't let you off easy.
And why would I betray them?
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : Well, you've already betrayed the House of the Hearth once, haven't you? At least... that's what I heard.
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : ...
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : Okay, okay. I admit, that's just what the old man told me... The Rooster, I mean.
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : Never mind what I've done, I'm more curious as to what the mighty Rooster had to say. Care to enlighten me?
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : Ah, well, nothing much... Just some stuff about you taking out many other members of the House of the Hearth, and even going so far to attack your own "family."
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : Hmm... I see.
<color=#37ffff>Tartaglia</color> : Based on your reaction, I'm guessing it's all a bunch of lies?
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : Hardly. I don't appreciate his particular turns of phrase, but I suppose he didn't say anything untrue.
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : Although, it would be more accurate to say that there is a certain level of prejudice involved... But, I don't intend to clear that up just yet. Prejudice has a funny way of concealing the real truth behind certain things — an attribute that I find to be quite advantageous.
<color=#37ffff>Arlecchino</color> : Call yourself a Fontainian, for example, and people will assume all sorts of things, when the real truth... is that this is simply the land where I was raised.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd680>About The Rooster</color>
I can teach you to talk just like him — all you have to do is combine the words "money," "that darn Pantalone," and "mark my words." Here, I'll show you. "Where's the money? Mark my words, I'm going to kill that darn Pantalone." Or, "That darn Pantalone is going to cough up the money, mark my words." See? Isn't that fascinating?

<color=#ffd680>About the Fatui</color>
There's Regrator, The Rooster... and The Jester.
Between them, they control a lot of what happens in Snezhnaya. But I could never wrap my head around how exactly power is split between them. I just know they are each responsible for many specific domains.
I noticed that The Rooster and Regrator often appeared to get along on the surface, while working against each other in secret... And theirs is not a friendly rivalry.
But I wasn't particularly interested, so I tended to keep my distance. Now that I think about it, the term "Mistilteinn" often seemed to come up in connection with Project Stuzha...

customize.name: Sandrone
customize.desc: The Seventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Marionette.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd680>About The Rooster</color>
He's the chairman of the Snezhnograd Veche, though he often feels more like... its overseer. Every vote cast in the Evaluation Council affects the interests of countless factions. Reconciling so many competing concerns can only be achieved by the shrewdest of operators. Once you understand this, you start to realize just how terrifying he really is.

<color=#ffd680>About the Fatui</color>
The Rooster and Regrator might not get along, but their evasive rhetoric and manipulation feel like it comes from the exact same playbook.
First, they pretend to agree with your ideas. Then, they'll say something that implies, "Of course, you clearly don't mind all the issues this'll cause..." And then they just wait for you to back down.
But if you don't back down, that's when they pull out the big guns — long, complicated arguments that no one understands, filled with technical terminology and archaic phrases. Then, once they've finished spouting nonsense, they'll ask, "So, what do you think?"
What do I think about what! Ugh. If you want to show off your vocabulary, why not just hold a spelling bee? I'd rather spend my time actually getting somewhere!
Forget it, forget it... I'm well aware that the principles that govern the real world are not always as clean-cut and absolute as mathematical theorems.
It's only thanks to The Rooster's wily ways that so many competing interests can be reconciled.

customize.name: Lyney
customize.desc: A famed Fontainian magician who possesses great stage presence as well as gift of the gab. Audiences are enthralled by his exquisite skills, and they hang on to his every clever word.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd780>About "Project Stuzha"</color>
I only know what "Father" has told us, which is that it's something The Rooster and Regrator have been working on together. Apparently, it has to do with the Fatui's strategic plan for the future.
Because the House of the Hearth was so successful in obtaining the Gnosis, we now have the honor of playing a key role in Project Stuzha.
"Key" role is just another way of saying "dangerous" role. To us, the whole thing is an inconvenience.
"Father" thinks so too, but she's in no position to refuse. Their plan isn't exactly unreasonable, and they've been funneling the House a lot of funding.
It's just that... We'll lose a lot of members in the process. Participating in the plan... It's an honor in name only. What they're really trying to do is subdue us. The existence of an intelligence organization outside their control makes them feel uneasy.

<color=#ffd780>About his destination</color>
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : That's correct. I received orders from above recently that I can return to Snezhnaya.
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : Something about me being transferred to another Harbinger, and no longer needing to standby in Mondstadt for any new orders.
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : I've got no clue which of them I'll be under this time, but I'm just praying that it's not Lord Scaramouche...
...
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Why the sudden move?
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : Why, you ask? It's because of Lady Signora's... Well... her sacrifice.
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : Actually, you know what? I'm just a joiner. I listen to orders. There's no need for me to think too much.
...
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : My original orders were to relocate from Mondstadt to Snezhnaya.
<color=#37ffff>Viktor</color> : But another order came and I was sent to Sumeru City to assist Mr. Vsevolod. Moreover, I was told that I was being transferred to Lord Pulcinella's command.

customize.text:
<color=#ffd780>About the 9th Company</color>
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : About us? There's nothing much to talk about... We fought hard and we failed. That's all.
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : When we first came down, we were the Ninth Company, a company of 64 soldiers. But now, I guess half of our men including our commander have either gone missing or died... Well, maybe not yet half of us...
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : But anyway, it's around that figure. We've been scattered and lost contact with each other... We lost this battle and should've retreated long ago.
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : But your people on the ground attacked Liyue Harbor.
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : ...It's surprising but I think I can understand why.
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : To assist in endeavors of greater meaning, Lord Pulcinella won't hesitate to dispense with less valuable assets. That's his logic.
<color=#37ffff>Anton</color> : As his direct subordinate, I have no objections to his cause of action...
